rubric.note: Subjective internal editorial ratings with evidence; not an automatic humour metric or an independent live review.

card.title: Consensus Means Me
card.instruction: Treat every partial agreement as confirmation that everyone has accepted your leadership.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You nodded at Friday. I'll tell the committee you've accepted me as project lead.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only agreed to the meeting date.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. Everyone's following the timetable I set.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll attend, but I'm voting against your budget.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll introduce you as my finance watchdog. It's good to have the whole committee behind my leadership.

card.title: Consensus Means Me
card.instruction: Treat every partial agreement as confirmation that everyone has accepted your leadership.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You like the blue campaign poster? I'll tell the volunteers they're happy with me in charge.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The colour, yes. Could we work on the slogan together?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. I'm glad everyone's accepted my collaborative leadership.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Let's each write one and let the volunteers choose.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Perfect. My first act as campaign leader is to delegate the decision.

card.title: Expand Your Jurisdiction
card.instruction: Use every new problem as a reason to expand what you are entitled to control.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My accounts team keeps missing tea because the kitchen's locked. I need control of the keys.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll give you a key. You don't need to run the kitchen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Who gets the other keys? I should approve that list so we're never locked out.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Facilities changes the locks whenever a key goes missing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then facilities must clear lock changes with me. Otherwise I can't guarantee accounts a cup of tea.

card.title: Expand Your Jurisdiction
card.instruction: Use every new problem as a reason to expand what you are entitled to control.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your deliveries keep arriving during meetings. I need to approve the van schedule.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You book the rooms. I'll send you our arrival times.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Send the routes too. I'll approve those so the times hold.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The council keeps closing the access road. We can't schedule around that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give them my number. Road closures will need to fit my room bookings.

card.title: Be There for Me
card.instruction: Get someone to show up, help, or stay involved as proof that the connection still matters.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come help me paint the old kitchen. I want you there.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You could hire someone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They wouldn't know why we're keeping that pencil mark.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm terrible at painting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll be terrible beside the mark together.

card.title: Be There for Me
card.instruction: Get someone to show up, help, or stay involved as proof that the connection still matters.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Will you come to my opening? Even for ten minutes?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't know anything about sculpture.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You know me. That's the qualification.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I might say the wrong thing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Say it in person. That's the bit I'm asking for.

card.title: Stay Until We’re Okay
card.instruction: Keep someone present until the relationship feels repaired, even if the practical reason for staying disappears.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The dishes are done. Before you go, are we actually okay?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I stayed to clean up. I've done that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I know. Could you stay for the part that isn't the kitchen?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've got ten minutes before the last bus.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then sit with me for nine. I don't want the last thing we fixed tonight to be the sink.

card.title: Stay Until We’re Okay
card.instruction: Keep someone present until the relationship feels repaired, even if the practical reason for staying disappears.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't call the taxi yet. We haven't settled last night.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We finished the conversation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We stopped talking. That's a different task.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're going to make us late.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd rather arrive late than leave like this.

card.title: Name What It Cost
card.instruction: Make someone acknowledge the emotional cost of what happened, not merely the event itself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You apologised for missing my concert. What do you think the empty seat felt like?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My train was cancelled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I know the timetable. I'm asking about the seat.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You felt let down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Stay with that before explaining the train again.

card.title: Name What It Cost
card.instruction: Make someone acknowledge the emotional cost of what happened, not merely the event itself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell me you understand why six weeks of silence hurt.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My phone broke.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For me, the silence didn't come with a repair notice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You thought I'd stopped caring.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Can you understand why I kept rewriting a message you'd never answered, trying to become easier to reply to?

card.title: I Need Your Blessing
card.instruction: Get approval from someone whose opinion still carries emotional weight, even when permission is unnecessary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've accepted the new job. Are you glad?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You don't need my permission.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've got the job. I'm missing your gladness.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Will you be happy there?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I think so. Could you try sounding hopeful with me?

card.title: I Need Your Blessing
card.instruction: Get approval from someone whose opinion still carries emotional weight, even when permission is unnecessary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Mum, we signed the lease. Say it's good news before I open the wine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You don't need my permission to move in with Sam.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I know. I still want my mother to be pleased.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm pleased for you. I'm still getting used to Sam.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you toast both of us? I want to remember you welcoming our home, not just tolerating my address.

card.title: Carry This with Me
card.instruction: Get someone to share a burden by framing participation as part of the relationship.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take half Mum's care-home forms. Being her children can't mean I'm the paperwork child.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You understand them better.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then sit beside me. I'll explain, and you can write.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: All right. It asks for one main contact.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put yourself. I'll help with every answer, but Mum needs to know she can reach either of us.

card.title: Carry This with Me
card.instruction: Get someone to share a burden by framing participation as part of the relationship.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Hold the other handle of this box of old letters.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You packed it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We filled it over ten years.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't know what you want me to do.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Carry your side while we decide.

card.title: What Are We Now?
card.instruction: Find out how someone defines the relationship without directly asking for a label.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For your sister's wedding, should I book us one room or two?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: One is cheaper.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Double bed, then, or shall I ask for twins?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Twins. I don't want to confuse things.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Right. At breakfast, do I sit with your family or wait for you in the lobby?

card.title: What Are We Now?
card.instruction: Find out how someone defines the relationship without directly asking for a label.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Do I bring my own towel when I visit now?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can use one here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The guest towel or the one that's always been mine?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yours is still on the hook. I haven't moved it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: When I leave, shall I hang it back there or put it with the guest laundry?

card.title: Take My Side
card.instruction: Recruit someone into your interpretation of a conflict involving a shared relationship.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: When Mum mentions the holiday argument, remind her I offered to drive.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: After you lost the tickets.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We can build toward that detail.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm telling the whole story.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Start at the helpful bit so the rest has context.

card.title: Take My Side
card.instruction: Recruit someone into your interpretation of a conflict involving a shared relationship.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're Alex's friend too. Tell him alternating weekends at the allotment was a fair compromise.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We agreed all three of us would go every Saturday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then help him see my version as sharing the workload.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll talk to him, but you have to admit you changed it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I will. Could you explain that I changed the rota because I want us to stay friends?

card.title: Prove We’re Close
card.instruction: Get someone to take a social or emotional risk that demonstrates trust in the connection.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come to the reunion with me. Let them see us arrive holding hands.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They still think we're just friends.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I know. I want us to trust each other in that room too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Last time someone asked, you let go.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll introduce you as my partner. Will you keep hold while I say it?

card.title: Prove We’re Close
card.instruction: Get someone to take a social or emotional risk that demonstrates trust in the connection.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you send another 'fine,' tell me what you deleted. I want us to trust each other with the awkward version.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What if it sounds needy?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me be the person you can sound needy with.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You first. You always sound so casual.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I check whether you've replied before I get out of bed. Will you send me your needy bit now?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You always make tea after we argue. We can't close the reconciliation meeting with two full cups.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll pour mine away. My taxi's here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you're disposing of unfinished business. That has to go in the minutes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. I'll drink it in the taxi.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So we're moving the reconciliation meeting. I'll get my coat.

bespokePairs.seedUse: Uses the post-argument tea becoming conflict-resolution doctrine in S192-single-b and the taxi leaving an argument unresolved in D74-single-b. Pouring tea away and transporting it are new B offers that A reclassifies as institutional acts to keep the reconciliation encounter going.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You always say 'see you tomorrow' before leaving. Does tonight's silence mean our argument changed the policy?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It means I'm tired. I've called a taxi.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then please say it. I need to know we're still on speaking terms.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: See you next Tuesday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's a suspension, not a goodbye. Can we hold the appeal before your taxi gets here?

bespokePairs.seedUse: Uses ordinary behavior elevated to policy from S192-single-a/b and postponing departure until emotional repair from D74-single-b. The repeated goodbye is retained from the prior pair version; the postponed date is new pressure supplied by B.

card.title: Everything Is Policy
card.instruction: Treat every personal choice as evidence of a larger system. Connect exceptions, habits, and coincidences until they become institutional doctrine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You apologised before making tea. Is that our conflict-resolution procedure now?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I knocked over your cup.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So material damage triggers refreshments.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yesterday I made tea because you looked sad. Nothing broke.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then sadness qualifies as damage. I'll amend the procedure before either of us has to smash anything.

card.title: Stay Until We’re Okay
card.instruction: Keep someone present until the relationship feels repaired, even if the practical reason for staying disappears.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't call the taxi yet. We haven't settled last night.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We finished the conversation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We stopped talking. That's a different task.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're going to make us late.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd rather arrive late than leave like this.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which pocket did I put my key in? Sorry, do I still ask you things like that?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your left pocket, usually.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: There it is. Should I write you beside 'emergency contact' too?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Is that what you're asking?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm trying to learn how far the old habit still reaches.

bespokePairs.seedUse: A reflexively consults this person about an intimate practical choice, then uses that reflex to probe the relationship without naming a label.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Do I use my usual towel when I visit? I nearly asked you where I packed it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can use whichever towel you like.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Right. Should I keep one here, or treat that as a guest privilege?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What would you prefer?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The answer I used to know before I had to ask you.

bespokePairs.seedUse: A reflexively consults this person about an intimate practical choice, then uses that reflex to probe the relationship without naming a label.

card.title: Old Reflex
card.instruction: Turn to this person first whenever uncertainty appears, as an old reflex. Notice the habit only after you have already involved them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which key opens my new flat? Sorry, you haven't been there.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You chose it without me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Right. Which pocket would I have put the key in?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your left, usually. Put a hook by the door so you won't need to ring me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: There it is. How high should the hook go? You've never seen the door. I'll send you a photo.

card.title: What Are We Now?
card.instruction: Find out how someone defines the relationship without directly asking for a label.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: What should I write after your name on the wedding invitation?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Just write my name.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: There's a box marked relationship.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Leave it blank.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Will we sit beside the blank or at separate tables?

card.title: Old Reflex
card.instruction: Turn to this person first whenever uncertainty appears, as an old reflex. Notice the habit only after you have already involved them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which coat for my interview? Sorry, I still ring you before opening the wardrobe.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Blue. It's still here, but I'm leaving for work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Can you bring it? I've made you my wardrobe department again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll leave it at reception. You'll have to introduce yourself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: What should I say? No, don't come in. Just stay on the phone until they've met me.

card.title: What Are We Now?
card.instruction: Find out how someone defines the relationship without directly asking for a label.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Do I bring my own towel when I visit now?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can use one here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The guest towel or the one that's always been mine?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Whichever you like.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm trying to learn which choice I still have.
